cases.exposure_context_quote: Five days prior to symptom onset, he had been applying a 1- to 2-thousand-fold dilution of imidacloprid pesticide to fruit trees. Accidentally, the pesticide entered his eye during application
cases.agent: imidacloprid pesticide (1- to 2-thousand-fold dilution), applied to fruit trees (NOTE: the Discussion inconsistently calls the agent 'pyraclostrobin')
cases.agent_quote: he had been applying a 1- to 2-thousand-fold dilution of imidacloprid pesticide to fruit trees
cases.circumstance: accidental eye contact while spraying pesticide on fruit trees; did not seek care at that time; treated at local clinic without improvement, then admitted

symptoms.finding: immediate burning and discomfort in the eye
symptoms.quote: When the pesticide spray inadvertently made contact with the patient’s eyes, they were seared with a burning sensation and discomfort.

symptoms.finding: diplopia in the right eye and difficulty opening the right eye (ptosis), from day 2 post-exposure
symptoms.quote: Subsequent to this incident, on the second day, the individual began to experience diplopia in the right eye and found it arduous to elevate his eyelids

symptoms.finding: right eye upward and rightward gaze restriction, conjunctival congestion, 3 mm pupil with diminished light reflexes
symptoms.quote: Notably, upward and rightward gazes were restricted in the right eye, accompanied by conjunctival congestion, a clear cornea, a round pupil measuring approximately 3 mm, diminished direct and consensual light reflexes
B-mode ultrasonography of both eyes indicated vitreous opacities, with no other remarkable findings (Fig. 1).

cases.time_to_care: symptoms persisted 4 days before admission; treated first at a local clinic without improvement (no interval given)

labs.name: complete blood count, liver and kidney function tests, chest CT, head CT, ECG
labs.quote: On the day of admission, routine examinations such as chest computed tomography (CT), head CT, electrocardiogram, complete blood count, and liver and kidney function tests were conducted and no obvious abnormalities were found.

labs.name: visual acuity
labs.quote: Ophthalmological evaluation revealed visual acuities of 1.0 in each eye.

treatment.name: intravenous dexamethasone (5 mg→10 mg→20 mg→5 mg daily escalation/de-escalation)
treatment.quote: dexamethasone 5 mg was administered intravenously once daily to reduce inflammatory response in the eye

treatment.name: pantoprazole enteric-coated tablets 40 mg orally once daily
treatment.quote: pantoprazole enteric-coated tablets 40 mg were given orally once daily to protect the stomach

treatment.name: Xuesaitong 400 mg IV once daily
treatment.quote: Xuesaitong 400 mg was administered intravenously once daily to improve blood supply to the eye and promote metabolism of toxic substances

treatment.name: vitamin C 2 g IV once daily
treatment.quote: vitamin C 2 g was injected intravenously once daily to nourish nerves

treatment.name: tobramycin-dexamethasone eye drops (local), continued at home after discharge
treatment.quote: tobramycin-dexamethasone eye drops were used locally to anti-inflammatory

treatment.name: repeated saline flushing of conjunctival sac
treatment.quote: the conjunctival sac was flushed repeatedly with saline

treatment.name: vitamin B1 0.1 g intramuscularly (twice/day)
treatment.quote: vitamin B1 0.1 g injected intramuscularly (twice/day) to nourish nerves

cases.outcome: improved (diplopia resolved and ptosis significantly improved); discharged day 7; at day-13 follow-up eyelid aperture equal to left eye
cases.outcome_quote: On the fifth day, the patient reported no diplopia and significant improvement in ptosis ... and the patient was discharged on the seventh day with instructions to continue using tobramycin-dexamethasone eye drops at home.
cases.sequelae: none reported; at follow-up the size of the right eyelid aperture was the same as that of the left eye
cases.notes: First reported case of oculomotor nerve palsy from this insecticide. Important inconsistency: title/abstract/case report name imidacloprid, but the entire Discussion section uses 'pyraclostrobin'. Article states acute conjunctivitis followed by a latent period before ptosis/diplopia.
